text:
**continue**: land CL44. Then, before the next full test run on this computer, put CL43 back to complete from git (board-mirror 5d7db0d) and launch CL48 ("a test never writes to the real board"), and make its prompt cover what overwrote CL43 on the live board at 20:24 UTC.

## Holds

**The step's own check, rerun on branch `cl44` at 411c4eb** (worktree /tmp/review-cl44-…): `python3 -m unittest tests.test_cl44_agy_runtime`: 20 tests, OK, 16.6 s. Matches the post's bar (20 of 20).

**The claim picked for a recheck: "live agy queue: 1 of 1 agy-assigned step shown, read through the worktree-safe relative MCP config."** I reran it rather than reread it:
- `.agents/mcp_config.json` on the branch runs `python3 -I .kit/mcp_stdio.py --root .`. That is relative, as claimed.
- I started that server exactly as the config says, with the cwd set to the review worktree (not the main checkout), and called `board_queue(runner="agy")` over stdio. It answered 1 card: `cl43-the-live-line-and-loop-breaker-on-agy (@agy train:cli/CL43)`. It no longer shows CL44 because CL44 is complete now. An independent count of the board's 94 posts finds 2 with runner agy: CL43 (planned) and CL44 (complete). So the queue shows every open agy step.
- **I saw the claim fail:** the same call with the config from before CL44 (e551381: absolute `/home/anon/board/.kit/mcp_stdio.py --root /home/anon/board`) answers `queue (runner=agy): 0 open cards`, because it reads a different checkout's board. The fix is what makes the difference.
- The script is kept: `scripts/review/CR-cl44-agy-runtime-startup-mcp-usage-and-mirror-fixes-agy-queue.py` (commit 27feb7c). Pass `CFG=<old config>` to see it fail.

**One cheap extra rerun:** `kit.py resume --cli agy` in the review worktree finished with rc 0 and no STALE refusal (item 1). Item 11 works: it names CL43's branch, worktree and last checkpoint ("branch `cl43` · last checkpoint `3902d1e`").

**What I did not check:** items 4 (usage row), 5 (`--mode auto`), 8–10 and 12, beyond their unit tests passing. I did not rerun the full suite or Harmonize. The post's own not_checked holds a real gap: piece 6 asked for a live `board --agy` run showing that update_steps ticks pieces (8), that the "failed to unmarshal" line from agy is gone (9), and that a checkpoint commit happens (10). That run was replaced by feeding one old transcript to the Stop hook. Items 8–10 were bugs seen in a live agy session, and no live agy session has run since the fix. No `asked` entries; breaks is `revert`, which I did for the claim above.

**Real project (K2):** the post's real_project is filled in. On Harmonize, install --update works, but `resume` on a computer is still refused by the Artifact STALE gate (rc 3), because Harmonize names an Artifact without `kit.mode local`. So item 1 holds here but not on the owner's real project. The post hands this to CL51 (planned, runner claude-web). That is fair, but it means an agy part on Harmonize still cannot start from resume today.

## Goal

The `cli` train serves one thing: a part runs, and its work is kept and seen, whatever CLI starts it (agy or Claude Code). Most of CL44 measures that directly: a part starts, sees its queue and records its cost. Two facts across the posts say the train's goal is not met yet:

1. **Item 7's failure came back on the live board, with CL44's code running.** CL44's item 7 was about losing CL43's completion (the 00:31 reconcile). The git copy shows CL43 complete at board-mirror 5d7db0d (20:01 UTC). Then the board's changes log has `posts/cl43-… set v4 at 2026-11-26T20:24:27Z`, actor `owner` with no session id. The next sync, 47cd73a "kit sync-db 2026-11-26T20:24:28Z", replaced it with the original plan: status planned, pieces open, and no verdict, bars, branch, commit or review fields. The board server had been running since 17:40 UTC (after CL44 merged at 17:08 UTC). The same batch (20:23:51–20:24:40) also `set` _dashboard, _orchestrator, _prefs, _trains, cl16, cl17, cl32, cl39, cl41, cl42 and four comments. I could not find which process wrote it: reading the other sessions' transcripts was refused, and I did not work around that. I have one hypothesis, not proved. 88b4f3a ("every checkout reaches the running board", 19:09 UTC) plus a test run at about that time (CL44 ran the suite between its 19:59 and 20:51 commits) could let a test write its fixtures into the real board. That is exactly what CL48 is planned to stop. It is not item 7's code path (that one is seed, reconcile and full sync; this is a plain `set`), so it does not make CL44 wrong. But the train's question, "is work ever lost?", still gets a yes.
2. **The loss now gives wrong guidance.** `resume` lists CL43 as "launched, died (… no live session)". CL43 was reviewed `continue` (cr-cl43-review), and its commit 3902d1e is on feat/streamline-doctor-memory. A fresh orchestrator reading this could relaunch a finished step.

**Known-good case:** the owner's own run of an agy part on Harmonize has not passed. Resume is refused there (above). **When the owner last tried it himself:** I found no comment from the owner on CL43 or CL44. The last three cli Dones (CL42, CL43, CL44) are all session-checked. By the rule, the next step after this landing is his own try of an agy part, once CL51 lets resume run on Harmonize.

## Verdict

**continue.** CL44 does what its post says: the check passes and the sampled claim passes on the new config and fails on the old one. Resume names where work is. Its open edges (the STALE gate on Harmonize, the live agy run for 8–10) are named honestly in the post and handed on.

**One suggestion for the orchestrator:** before any other full test run on this computer, restore CL43's post from board-mirror 5d7db0d (status complete, review continue, review_id cr-cl43-review). Then launch CL48 with a prompt that says this: "the board's changes log shows a batch of `set`s at 2026-11-26T20:23:51–20:24:40Z, actor owner with no session id, that replaced CL43 (complete) and 10 other documents with older copies. Find the writer, and make that write impossible from a test or a checkout other than the board's own, with a test that fails on today's code."
